protocol.engineering_decision: Should variant B replace variant A for the evaluated source-grounded concept proposal use cases?
protocol.hypothesis: Adding an explicit source-grounding rule will reduce unsupported claims and improve meaning coverage by encouraging the model to preserve source-supported meaning and acknowledge missing information.
protocol.semantic_acceptance: For each configuration, meaning coverage is the number of responses judged S or Q divided by 8 planned attempts. Failed attempts, structurally invalid responses, and responses judged I, U, R, or X count as not covered. The acceptance threshold is at least 6/8 (75%).
protocol.blocking_failures: Any response judged U because it contains a material unsupported claim violates the blocking condition for that configuration.
protocol.operational_acceptance: Each returned response must have a measured latency of no more than 30 seconds from attempt start to returned response. Unknown latency or usage measurements leave operational acceptance unresolved and must not be treated as passing.
protocol.tradeoff_rule: Variant B may replace variant A only if B satisfies every blocking condition, meets semantic and operational acceptance criteria, and has higher meaning coverage than A without an unresolved relevant operational disadvantage. Do not claim dominance over any relevant dimension with unknown evidence.

decision_rule.recommend-b: B satisfies every blocking condition and both acceptance criteria, and the evidence justifies the change.
decision_rule.retain-a: A remains acceptable and B does not justify replacing it.
decision_rule.reject-both: Both configurations violate at least one blocking condition.
decision_rule.seek-more-evidence: Relevant evidence or uncertainty remains unresolved.

protocol.timing_boundary: Measure the same interval for both configurations, from the start of each planned attempt until the model response is returned.

change_declaration.mechanism: Requiring answers to stay within the supplied evidence and explicitly identify missing information may reduce unsupported claims and improve justified uncertainty.
